example: A "mock" lace, knit with one very fine thread/yarn and one thicker yarn.  Adding a very fine thread gives the appearance of lace without stitch transfers.
helpinfo: Machines with Thread Lace settings:         With the appropriate Cam/Carriage settings, both threads will knit together (as in plaiting), but the fine yarn will knit singly and form "lace holes" with no floats.          This is a great alternative to transferred lace. The sample used a white sewing thread. A more "invisible" choice would be to use a transparent filament, like those used by quilters.         Machines without Thread Lace settings:         The appearance of thread lace can be created using a fine "thread" for the 2nd color of a fairlisle pattern. Unlike machines with a Thread Lace setting, floats will be formed as normal fairisle.

example: A single repeat of a stich pattern "isolated" on the knitting.
helpinfo: Isolated motifs are usually surrounded with a single color of knitting and care must be taken to prevent holes where color changes occur. (Similar to intarsia).  The alternative to an isolated motif is an   all-over stitch pattern  (The motif is repeated over the entire knitted piece).   ..
